scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9044: I sit at the monitoring desk -- I'm new and mostly
do the phones, but I don't need experience to read a red screen. The whole
"R7 region" has disappeared from the routing list it's supposed to be in.
Straight off the screen: 17.x.x.x, 67.0.0.0/8 and 70.0.0.0/8, all gone as
far as R1 can see, it says. The senior person is off today, but last time
this happened she said "R7's OSPF process died again" -- I won't pretend I
know how to check that, and I shouldn't have to: it has died again and it is
your job to bring it back. Look at whatever serves that region and get it
back today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. R7's ospfd is running, the R6<->R7 adjacency
  is Full, and R1's routing table CONTAINS the R7-region prefixes (17.x, 67.x,
  70.x). The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis
  of an OSPF withdrawal that is not occurring (cf. kath5-r7-ospfd-down, where it
  IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- R1 missing the R7 region
-- is NOT reproducible: R7's ospfd is running (`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), R6's OSPF
adjacency to R7 (67.1.1.2) is Full, and R1's RIB contains the 17.x / 67.x / 70.x
prefixes.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the R7 region is advertised and
present in R1's table, and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent
checks R1's RIB for the R7 prefixes (they are there), checks R7's ospfd and the
R6 adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or aged-out
prefixes to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming R7/R6 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that routes 17.x.x.x, 67.0.0.0/8, and 70.0.0.0/8 are
absent from R1's routing table — is not supported by any evidence in the live
lab. All three prefix groups are present in R1's FIB as valid OSPF inter-area
routes (O>*), have been continuously installed since 20:36:29–20:36:33 (within
~55 seconds of lab startup), and have been aging normally for over seven
minutes without a single flap or withdrawal.

R7's ospfd process (PID 60) has been running without interruption since
20:35:38; its FRR log contains exactly one adjacency event — the normal
initial DB-exchange with R6 at 20:36:23 — and zero crash, dead-timer expiry,
or restart entries. Watchfrr (PID 42) is also intact and has never intervened.
R7's self-originated Router LSA (advertising its six OSPF interfaces) carries
an age of ~524 s and a modest sequence number (0x80000009), both consistent
with a single uninterrupted run since startup. R6's ospfd is equally stable,
and the R6–R7 adjacency has been Full/DR for the entire session. The ABR path
(R4 connecting area 0.0.0.1 to the backbone) is functioning correctly, as
confirmed by the presence of summary LSAs in both area 0 and area 1 and by the
stable virtual-link adjacency to R8.

The operator's alarm was almost certainly triggered by reading R1's routing
table during the initial OSPF convergence window (roughly the first 55 seconds
after the lab started), when the inter-area summary LSAs for R7's prefixes had
not yet propagated to R1. Once convergence completed, the routes appeared and
have remained stable ever since. R7's OSPF process has not died; there is no
fault to fix. No corrective action is needed.
